subaward_description: 1 THE INDIVIDUAL TECHNICAL DIRECTION WILL INDICATE WHETHER THE TASKS WILL BE PERFORMED AT CONTRACTOR OR GOVERNMENT FACILITIES. FOR EACH TECHNICAL DIRECTION ISSUED UNDER THIS CONTRACT, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PREPARE STATUS REPORTS AND FUNDS AND MAN-HOUR EXPENDITURE REPORTS. A STATUS REPORT SHALL BE PREPARED AND DELIVERED IN ACCORDANCE WITH (IAW) DI-MGMT-80368, CONTRACT DATA REQUIREMENT LIST (CDRL) A001. A  CONTRACTORÃ¯Â¿Â½S PROGRESS STATUS AND MANAGEMENT REPORT SHALL BE PREPARED AND DELIVERED IAW DI-MGMT-80227, CDRL A003. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL BE REQUIRED TO ATTEND QUARTERLY MEETINGS TO ASSESS THE STATUS AND PROGRESS OF THE TECHNICAL DIRECTION.

subaward_description: 1 THE INDIVIDUAL TECHNICAL DIRECTION WILL INDICATE WHETHER THE TASKS WILL BE PERFORMED AT CONTRACTOR OR GOVERNMENT FACILITIES. A  CONTRACTORÃ¯Â¿Â½S PROGRESS STATUS AND MANAGEMENT REPORT SHALL BE PREPARED AND DELIVERED IAW DI-MGMT-80227, CDRL A003. subaward_description:
THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE TECHNICAL EXPERTISE TO MEET MISSION REQUIREMENTS OF THE SYSTEMS AND
WARHEADS FUNCTION, PROPULSION AND STRUCTURES DIVISION, WEAPONS DEVELOPMENT AND INTEGRATION (WDI)
DIRECTORATE, COMBAT CAPABILITIES DEVELOPMENT COMMAND AVMC (CCDC AVMC). MISSION REQUIREMENTS
TO BE SUPPORTED CONSIST OF, WARHEAD DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT, ANALYSIS; MODELING, FABRICATION, PRODUCTION, TEST
AND EVALUATION FOR MISSILE AND ROCKET SYSTEMS; INTEGRATION OF LETHAL MECHANISMS ON SYSTEMS TO INCLUDE
ANTI-ARMOR, AIR DEFENSE, MILITARY OPERATIONS IN URBAN TERRAIN (MOUT), HYPERVELOCITY AND OTHER
TECHNOLOGY TEST BED DEMONSTRATIONS IN SUPPORT OF THE AMCOM MISSION; AIR AND GROUND SYSTEMS DESIGN
AND TESTING; FUZING SUPPORT IN THE AREAS OF ELECTRONIC AND MECHANICAL SAFE AND ARM DEVICES AND TARGET
DETECTION SYSTEMS, AND COMPOSITES AND MATERIALS FOR MISSILE AND AVIATION SYSTEMS.

subaward_description:
STATEMENT OF WORK
THIS SUBAWARD SERVES TWO PURPOSES: 1) ESTABLISH AN INTERIOR ALASKA FIELD SITE WITH A
COMPREHENSIVE SNOW AND SLOPE STABILITY RESEARCH PROGRAM AND 2) CONTRIBUTE TO WORK ON THE
JUNEAU ICEFIELD
1) WE WILL ESTABLISH A FIELD SITE IN THE ALASKA RANGE TO COMPARE SNOW PACK EVOLUTION IN A DRY
INTERIOR CLIMATE TO THAT OF THE OTHER PROPOSED FIELD SITES IN SOUTHEAST ALASKA AND THE NORTHEASTERN
COAST OF MAINE. THE SITE IS LOCATED NEAR THE CANWELL GLACIER AND IS ACCESSIBLE YEAR ROUND VIA THE
RICHARDSON HIGHWAY AND, IN THE WINTER, VIA SNOW MACHINE. OUR PROPOSED SITE INCLUDES A
PERIGLACIAL ENVIRONMENT, STAGNANT DEBRIS COVERED ICE, AND A MOUNTAIN SLOPE WITH A KNOWN
LANDSLIDE INSTABILITY.
WE WILL CONDUCT REGULAR FIELD VISITS WITH THE GOAL OF MONITORING THE SNOW PACK DURING THE WINTER
AND PARTICULARLY DURING THE SPRING MELT SEASON AS WATER BECOMES AN IMPORTANT FACTOR. THE
MONITORING WILL OCCUR VIA REGULAR UNCREWED AERIAL VEHICLE (UAV) SURVEYS WITH A REGULAR CAMERA
FOR THE GENERATION OF ACCURATE DIGITAL ELEVATION MODELS, AND A HYPERSPECTRAL CAMERA FOR
CHARACTERIZING THE SNOW CONDITIONS. SNOW CONDITIONS WILL ALSO BE MONITORED WITH A TERRESTRIAL
RADAR INTERFEROMETER (TRI). UAF OWNS AND OPERATES A GAMMA REMOTE SENSING TRI THAT HAS
BEEN USED FOR THE STUDY OF UNSTABLE SLOPES, LANDSLIDES, AND GLACIER FLOW. THE INSTRUMENT CONSISTS
OF ONE TRANSMITTING AND TWO RECEIVING ANTENNAS. THE TWO RECEIVING ANTENNAS ALLOW THE
CONSTRUCTION OF DIGITAL ELEVATION MODELS (DEMS). THE INSTRUMENT WILL BE USED TO DOCUMENT
CHANGES IN REFLECTED RADAR ENERGY, AS THE SNOW PACK EVOLVES. FURTHERMORE WE WILL EXPLORE THE
UTILITY OF THE INSTRUMENT TO DOCUMENT RADAR PENETRATION DEPTH, WHICH WOULD MANIFEST AS PHASE
DIFFERENCES IN THE REFLECTED RADAR WAVE.
WE WILL SUPPLEMENT THE UAV AND TRI SURVEYS WITH GROUND MEASUREMENTS, INCLUDING A
COMPREHENSIVE WEATHER STATION AND SETS OF THERMISTOR STRINGS TO MONITOR SNOW AND SUBSURFACE
TEMPERATURE EVOLUTION DURING THE WINTER AND THE PERIOD OF SNOW MELT.
2) WE WILL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN WORK ON THE JUNEAU ICEFIELD. WE PLAN THREE SURVEY FLIGHTS EACH
WINTER WITH A HIGHLY ACCURATE RIEGL LIDAR. IN ADDITION, WE WILL CARRY OUT TRI SURVEYS (AS OUTLINED
ABOVE) TO ESTABLISH A PARALLEL PROGRAM TO OUR INTERIOR AK SITE.
THE UAF TEAM WILL CONSIST OF THE MAIN INVESTIGATOR TRUFFER WHO WILL COORDINATE ALL ACTIVITIES AND
PARTICIPATE IN FIELD WORK AND DATA ANALYSIS AT BOTH SITES, WITH A PARTICULAR EMPHASIS ON THE TRI
WORK. CO-I LARSEN AND A TECHNICIAN WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR ALL LIDAR MEASUREMENTS TO THE
PRODUCTION OF DEMS. CO-I PETERSEN WILL AND A GRADUATE STUDENT WHO WILL TAKE A LEADING ROLE IN
ESTABLISHING THE INTERIOR FIELD SITE AND THE WORK TO BE CONDUCTED THERE. A POST-DOCTORAL FELLOW WITH
EXPERTISE IN SNOW SCIENCE WILL BE HIRED FOR THE PROJECT AND ASSIST WITH ALL ASPECTS.
ALL PERSONNEL WILL COLLABORATE WITH THE OVERALL PROJECT INVESTIGATORS AND WILL ATTEND ANNUAL
WORKSHOPS IN MAINE.

subaward_description:
DARPA/I2OS COMPARTMENTALIZATION AND PRIVILEGE MANAGEMENT, CPM, PROGRAMS FOCUS IS ON SECURING THE 
VULNERABLE LEGACY CODE BASE. COMPLEMENTARY SOFTWARE AND HARDWARE SOLUTIONS ARE SOUGHT THAT WILL 
MAKE IT ECONOMICALLY VIABLE TO COMPARTMENTALIZE LEGACY SOFTWARE AROUND LEAST- PRIVILEGE PRINCIPLES 
WHILE ALSO DEMONSTRATING A HARDWARE ROADMAP THAT ENABLES PERFORMANT IMPLEMENTATION.
CPM IS PARTITIONED INTO THREE TECHNICAL AREAS (TAS): 1) AUTOMATED COMPARTMENTALIZATION, 2) 
PRIVILEGE POLICY ENFORCEMENT, AND 3) EVALUATION SUPPORT. A NEW SOLICITATION FOR A FOURTH TECHNICAL 
AREA, TA4: DOD SYSTEM EXPERIMENTATION, IS ANTICIPATED PRIOR TO PHASE 2, AFTER THE PROGRAM IS WELL 
UNDERWAY.
TA1 PERFORMERS WILL DEVELOP SOFTWARE ANALYSIS TOOLS THAT AUTOMATICALLY RESTRUCTURE LEGACY SOFTWARE 
SYSTEMS. THE RESTRUCTURED SYSTEM SHOULD CONTAIN FINE-GRAINED COMPARTMENTS AND ACCESS CONTROL RULES 
THAT LIMIT PRIVILEGES TO JUST THOSE NEEDED TO PERFORM THEIR TASK. THE RESTRUCTURED SYSTEM WILL ALSO 
RESTRICT THE TRANSITIONS BETWEEN EXECUTION CONTEXTS (I.E., PRINCIPALS) TO ONLY THOSE NEEDED.
TA2 PERFORMERS SHOULD DEVELOP PROCESSOR ARCHITECTURES AND SYSTEM SOFTWARE THAT WILL, WITH LOW 
OVERHEAD, ENFORCE COMPARTMENT AND PRIVILEGE MANAGEMENT PROTOCOLS DISCOVERED BY TA1 TOOLS TO PREVENT 
INITIAL PENETRATIONS FROM PROPAGATING INTO SUCCESSFUL CYBER-ATTACKS.
CPM IS PLANNED AS A 48-MONTH PROGRAM WITH A 30-MONTH PHASE 1 AND AN 18-MONTH PHASE 2. PHASE 1 WILL 
FOCUS ON TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT, SPECIFICALLY USING A UNIX-LIKE OS SUCH AS LINUX AS THE TEST AND 
EVALUATION SUITE. PHASE 2 WILL FOCUS ON SCALING THE TECHNOLOGIES AND WILL ADD USER- SPACE PROGRAMS 
TO THE TEST AND EVALUATION SUITE.
MORE DETAILED BACKGROUND REGARDING CPM GOALS AND REQUIREMENTS ARE PROVIDED IN DARPA/I2O BAA 
#HR0011-23-S-0028, AMENDMENT 1, DATED 13-APR-2023.
THE CHARLES STARK DRAPER LABORATORY, INC. (DRAPER) PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED THE PROCESSOR INTERLOCKS 
FOR POLICY ENFORCEMENT (PIPE) ARCHITECTURE THAT IMPLEMENTS SOME OF THE REQUIREMENTS FOR TA-1, 
AUTOMATED COMPARTMENTALIZATION, AND ESTABLISHES A FRAMEWORK FOR TA-
2, PRIVILEGE POLICY ENFORCEMENT.

subaward_description: DROP-STITCH MANUFACTURING IMPROVEMENTS TO INCREASE PRODUCTION RATE AND PRODUCT PERFORMANCE. DROP-STITCH PRESENTS UNIQUE CHALLENGES TO TRADITIONAL COATED FABRIC MANUFACTURING EQUIPMENT AND TECHNIQUES. AS AN EMERGING TECHNOLOGY, DROP-STITCH REQUIRES INNOVATIONS IN MANUFACTURING TO BE SUCCESSFULLY ADOPTED AND APPLIED. RECREATIONAL SECTOR DROP-STITCH DOES NOT MEET THE BERRY AMENDMENT REQUIREMENT AND THE FABRICATION PROCESS DOES NOT SCALE TO THE SIZE OF THE PANELS NEEDED FOR THE IV. THERE ARE CURRENTLY NO SOLUTIONS FOR RELIABLY AND REPEATABLY WELDING THERMOPLASTIC POLYURETHANE (TPU) DROP-STITCH PANELS IN A COST-EFFECTIVE MANNER. SOME EQUIPMENT AND TECHNIQUES USED ON SIMILARLY COATED FABRICS CAN BE USED AS A STARTING POINT TO TACKLE THE PROBLEMS OF MATERIAL HANDLING, ALIGNMENT, SENSING, HEAT SOURCE, PRESSURE APPLICATION, ETC. DROP-STITCH TECHNOLOGY IS STILL YOUNG AND HAS MANY UNKNOWNS, SO INDUSTRY PARTNERS DO NOT HAVE THE CAPABILITY TO IMPLEMENT ON THEIR OWN.

subaward_description: 1 THE INDIVIDUAL TECHNICAL DIRECTION WILL INDICATE WHETHER THE TASKS WILL BE PERFORMED AT CONTRACTOR OR GOVERNMENT FACILITIES. FOR EACH TECHNICAL DIRECTION ISSUED UNDER THIS CONTRACT, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PREPARE STATUS REPORTS AND FUNDS AND MAN-HOUR EXPENDITURE REPORTS. A STATUS REPORT SHALL BE PREPARED AND DELIVERED IN ACCORDANCE WITH (IAW) DI-MGMT-80368, CONTRACT DATA REQUIREMENT LIST (CDRL) A001. A  CONTRACTORÃ¯Â¿Â½S PROGRESS STATUS AND MANAGEMENT REPORT SHALL BE PREPARED AND DELIVERED IAW DI-MGMT-80227, CDRL A003. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL BE REQUIRED TO ATTEND QUARTERLY MEETINGS TO ASSESS THE STATUS AND PROGRESS OF THE TECHNICAL DIRECTION.

A  CONTRACTORÃ¯Â¿Â½S PROGRESS STATUS AND MANAGEMENT REPORT SHALL BE PREPARED AND DELIVERED IAW DI-MGMT-80227, CDRL A003. ANNIE BOUCHER (FOUNDATION FOR GLACIER & ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH)
THE PURPOSE OF THIS SUBAWARD IS FOR THE FOUNDATION FOR GLACIER & ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH (FGER) TO PROVIDE LOGISTICAL SUPPORT, FACILITIES USE, AND FIELD EQUIPMENT RESOURCES ON THE JUNEAU ICEFIELD IN SUPPORT OF THE RESEARCH CONDUCTED ON THIS PROJECT.  FGER MAINTAINS TEN FIELD STATIONS ACROSS 2000 KM2 OF THE JUNEAU ICEFIELD IN ALASKA AND CANADA.  THE FIELD CAMPS ARE HELICOPTER ACCESSIBLE YEAR-ROUND AND CAN ALSO BE ACCESSED FROM CAMP-TO-CAMP BY SNOW MACHINE OR TRACK VEHICLE DURING THE SPRING AND SUMMER (MARCH-AUGUST). JIRP ALSO OPERATES AN ANNUAL FIELD RESEARCH AND EDUCATION PROGRAM JUNE-AUGUST WITH OVER 40 UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS AND ANOTHER 40-50 SCIENTISTS AND EDUCATORS.  THIS FIELD PROGRAM PROVIDES AMPLE OPPORTUNITIES FOR COLLABORATION BETWEEN SCIENTISTS FROM DIFFERENT INSTITUTIONS AND LEARNING AND PARTICIPATION IN SCIENCE RESEARCH BY STUDENTS.  THIS PROJECT CLOSELY ALIGNS WITH FGER ANNUAL FIELD RESEARCH PROGRAMS. AS PART OF THIS PROJECT, FGER INTENDS TO SUPPORT IN-SITU DATA COLLECTION ON THE JUNEAU ICEFIELD BY:
1.	PROVIDING LODGING, MEALS, SCHEDULING OF ON AND OFF-ICE TRANSPORT BY HELICOPTER, SUPPORTING SAFETY PLANNING AND TRAINING, AND PROVIDING LOGISTICAL SUPPORT IN JUNEAU BASED ON THEIR DECADES OF EXPERIENCE WITH GLACIOLOGICAL RESEARCH ON THE ICEFIELD (NOTE, HELICOPTER EXPENSES ARE NOT WITHIN THIS BUDGET AND FALL UNDER UMAINE REQUIREMENTS), 
2.	LOANING ADDITIONAL SNOW MACHINES, GENERATORS, TENTS, EMERGENCY EQUIPMENT OR SNOW MACHINE TRAVERSES, AND OTHER FIELD EQUIPMENT AS NEEDED,
3.	PROVIDING ACCESS TO TWO MECHANICS SHOPS AT TWO OF THE LARGEST FIELD STATIONS AND ADDITIONAL MECHANIC/TECHNICIAN SUPPORT FOR THE PROJECT TO ASSURE FIELD SUCCESS IN THE EVENT HARDWARE OR EQUIPMENT REQUIRES MAINTENANCE WHILE IN THE FIELD, 
4.	PROVIDING ADDITIONAL FIELD PERSONNEL (UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS, GRADUATE STUDENTS, AND PARTICIPATING FACULTY WHO ARE PART OF THE PRIMARY JIRP PROGRAM) TO SUPPORT THE FIELD RESEARCH EQUIPMENT SETUP, MONITORING, DATA COLLECTION, AND DATA RETRIEVAL.

THE PURPOSE OF THIS SUBAWARD IS FOR DR. RIVERMAN AND TWO UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS PER YEAR TO

SURFACE AND SNOWPACK STABILITY. SHE WILL WORK WITH LEEMAN GEOPHYSICAL TO DESIGN AND BUILD NOVEL
THERMISTOR SENSORS FOR MONITORING GROUND TEMPERATURE AND CALCULATING THERMAL CONDUCTIVITY OF THE
NEAR SURFACE GEOLOGY. FROM ACTIVE SOURCE SEISMIC DATA SHE WILL MEASURE ACTIVE LAYER DEPTH OF
PERMAFROST. PASSIVE SEISMIC DATA WILL PROVIDE MONITORING FOR SLUMPING EVENTS, WHICH WILL BE

QUANTIFYING SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL VARIABILITY OF TEMPERATE SNOWPACK PROPERTIES USING
COUPLED RADAR, REMOTE SENSING, AND MODELING TECHNIQUES
DR. KIYA RIVERMAN (UNIVERSITY OF PORTLAND)
THE PURPOSE OF THIS SUBAWARD IS FOR DR. RIVERMAN AND TWO UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS PER YEAR TO
PROVIDE SEISMIC TECHNICAL EXPERTISE, INSTRUMENTATION, DATA COLLECTION, DATA PROCESSING, AND GENERAL
INTELLECTUAL CONTRIBUTIONS TO THE RESEARCH CONDUCTED ON THIS PROJECT.
AS PART OF THIS PROJECT, DR. RIVERMAN WILL:
1. COLLECT ACTIVE-SOURCE SEISMIC DATA
2. COLLECT PASSIVE-SOURCE SEISMIC DATA
3. COLLECT THERMAL DATA AT DEPTH (THERMISTOR STRINGS)
4. COLLABORATE IN THE INTEGRATION OF THE ABOVE DATASETS WITH THE OTHER DATASETS COLLECTED ON THIS
PROJECT
DR. RIVERMAN IN PARTICULAR WILL USE A COMBINATION OF GEOPHYSICAL TECHNIQUES TO DESCRIBE GROUND
STABILITY AND THE LIKELIHOOD FOR AVALANCHES AND GROUND SLUMPING AS SUMMER TEMPERATURES ACROSS
THE ICEFIELD RISE. RIVERMAN WILL USE ACTIVE AND PASSIVE SOURCE SEISMIC TECHNIQUES TO DESCRIBE NEAR
SURFACE AND SNOWPACK STABILITY. SHE WILL WORK WITH LEEMAN GEOPHYSICAL TO DESIGN AND BUILD NOVEL
THERMISTOR SENSORS FOR MONITORING GROUND TEMPERATURE AND CALCULATING THERMAL CONDUCTIVITY OF THE
NEAR SURFACE GEOLOGY. FROM ACTIVE SOURCE SEISMIC DATA SHE WILL MEASURE ACTIVE LAYER DEPTH OF
PERMAFROST. PASSIVE SEISMIC DATA WILL PROVIDE MONITORING FOR SLUMPING EVENTS, WHICH WILL BE
TRIANGULATED. THIS WORK WILL RESULT IN IMPROVED PREDICTIVE POWER FOR DESCRIBING WHEN AND WHERE
GROUND FAILURES WILL OCCUR. THE WIDESPREAD SCOPE OF THE PROJECT (GENERALLY FOCUSED ON LANDSCAPE
CHANGE IN A WARMING WORLD) INVOLVES A LARGE SUITE OF OBSERVATIONS ACROSS MULTIPLE INSTITUTIONS. DR.
RIVERMANÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S STUDENTS WILL BENEFIT FROM COLLABORATION WITH RESEARCHERS ACROSS THIS LARGE MULTIINSTITUTION
EFFORT. DR. RIVERMANÃ¢Â‚¬Â„¢S STUDENTS EACH SUMMER WILL FULLY PARTICIPATE IN THE JUNEAU ICEFIELD
RESEARCH PROGRAM AND ASSIST IN ALL DATA COLLECTION FOR THE PROJECT THAT OCCURS AS PART OF THE PROGRAM.
IN ADDITION, THEY WILL PARTICIPATE IN DATA PROCESSING AND ANALYSIS AFTER THE JIRP EXPEDITION AND
PRESENT THE RESULTS OF THEIR WORK AT AGU MEETINGS IN YEARS 2 AND 4.

subaward_description:
STATEMENT OF WORK
THIS SUBAWARD SERVES TWO PURPOSES: 1) ESTABLISH AN INTERIOR ALASKA FIELD SITE WITH A
COMPREHENSIVE SNOW AND SLOPE STABILITY RESEARCH PROGRAM AND 2) CONTRIBUTE TO WORK ON THE
JUNEAU ICEFIELD
1) WE WILL ESTABLISH A FIELD SITE IN THE ALASKA RANGE TO COMPARE SNOW PACK EVOLUTION IN A DRY
INTERIOR CLIMATE TO THAT OF THE OTHER PROPOSED FIELD SITES IN SOUTHEAST ALASKA AND THE NORTHEASTERN
COAST OF MAINE. THE SITE IS LOCATED NEAR THE CANWELL GLACIER AND IS ACCESSIBLE YEAR ROUND VIA THE
RICHARDSON HIGHWAY AND, IN THE WINTER, VIA SNOW MACHINE. OUR PROPOSED SITE INCLUDES A
PERIGLACIAL ENVIRONMENT, STAGNANT DEBRIS COVERED ICE, AND A MOUNTAIN SLOPE WITH A KNOWN
LANDSLIDE INSTABILITY.
WE WILL CONDUCT REGULAR FIELD VISITS WITH THE GOAL OF MONITORING THE SNOW PACK DURING THE WINTER
AND PARTICULARLY DURING THE SPRING MELT SEASON AS WATER BECOMES AN IMPORTANT FACTOR. THE
MONITORING WILL OCCUR VIA REGULAR UNCREWED AERIAL VEHICLE (UAV) SURVEYS WITH A REGULAR CAMERA
FOR THE GENERATION OF ACCURATE DIGITAL ELEVATION MODELS, AND A HYPERSPECTRAL CAMERA FOR
CHARACTERIZING THE SNOW CONDITIONS. SNOW CONDITIONS WILL ALSO BE MONITORED WITH A TERRESTRIAL
RADAR INTERFEROMETER (TRI). UAF OWNS AND OPERATES A GAMMA REMOTE SENSING TRI THAT HAS
BEEN USED FOR THE STUDY OF UNSTABLE SLOPES, LANDSLIDES, AND GLACIER FLOW. THE INSTRUMENT CONSISTS
OF ONE TRANSMITTING AND TWO RECEIVING ANTENNAS. THE TWO RECEIVING ANTENNAS ALLOW THE
CONSTRUCTION OF DIGITAL ELEVATION MODELS (DEMS). THE INSTRUMENT WILL BE USED TO DOCUMENT
CHANGES IN REFLECTED RADAR ENERGY, AS THE SNOW PACK EVOLVES. FURTHERMORE WE WILL EXPLORE THE
UTILITY OF THE INSTRUMENT TO DOCUMENT RADAR PENETRATION DEPTH, WHICH WOULD MANIFEST AS PHASE
DIFFERENCES IN THE REFLECTED RADAR WAVE.
WE WILL SUPPLEMENT THE UAV AND TRI SURVEYS WITH GROUND MEASUREMENTS, INCLUDING A
COMPREHENSIVE WEATHER STATION AND SETS OF THERMISTOR STRINGS TO MONITOR SNOW AND SUBSURFACE
TEMPERATURE EVOLUTION DURING THE WINTER AND THE PERIOD OF SNOW MELT.
2) WE WILL ALSO PARTICIPATE IN WORK ON THE JUNEAU ICEFIELD. WE PLAN THREE SURVEY FLIGHTS EACH
WINTER WITH A HIGHLY ACCURATE RIEGL LIDAR. IN ADDITION, WE WILL CARRY OUT TRI SURVEYS (AS OUTLINED
ABOVE) TO ESTABLISH A PARALLEL PROGRAM TO OUR INTERIOR AK SITE.
THE UAF TEAM WILL CONSIST OF THE MAIN INVESTIGATOR TRUFFER WHO WILL COORDINATE ALL ACTIVITIES AND
PARTICIPATE IN FIELD WORK AND DATA ANALYSIS AT BOTH SITES, WITH A PARTICULAR EMPHASIS ON THE TRI
WORK. CO-I LARSEN AND A TECHNICIAN WILL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR ALL LIDAR MEASUREMENTS TO THE
PRODUCTION OF DEMS. CO-I PETERSEN WILL AND A GRADUATE STUDENT WHO WILL TAKE A LEADING ROLE IN
ESTABLISHING THE INTERIOR FIELD SITE AND THE WORK TO BE CONDUCTED THERE. A POST-DOCTORAL FELLOW WITH
EXPERTISE IN SNOW SCIENCE WILL BE HIRED FOR THE PROJECT AND ASSIST WITH ALL ASPECTS.
ALL PERSONNEL WILL COLLABORATE WITH THE OVERALL PROJECT INVESTIGATORS AND WILL ATTEND ANNUAL
WORKSHOPS IN MAINE.

MISSION. THE MISSION INVOLVES CLEARING A SAFE PASSAGE THROUGH A MINEFIELD USING AUTONOMOUS GROUND AND AERIAL VEHICLES, REMOTE SENSING, AND AN AI DETECTION MODEL WHOSE ACCURACY CAN VARY WITH TYPE OF TERRAIN, TOPOGRAPHY, SEASON AND LIGHTING CONDITIONS. HUMAN SUBJECT MATTER EXPERTS CAN ALSO REVIEW IMAGERY TO DETECT MINES, WITH BETTER ACCURACY IN SOME CASES, BUT CANNOT ASSESS THE IMAGERY AS QUICKLY AS THE AI MODEL. FOR THE FIRST SEMESTER, THE UNMANNED GROUND VEHICLE (UGV) IS 100 PERCENT EFFECTIVE AT DETECTING AND CLEARING MINES, THOUGH THAT CONDITION MAY BE RELAXED IN FUTURE STAGES. THE STUDENT TEAMS HAVE BEEN PROVIDED WITH SYSML MODELS OF THE CONCEPT OF OPERATIONS, USE CASES, AND BLOCK DEFINITION DIAGRAMS OF THE SYSTEM ELEMENTS AND ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS. THE OVERALL TIME NEEDED TO CHART AND CLEAR A SAFE PASSAGE THROUGH THE TERRAIN IS THE PRIMARY MEASURE OF EFFECTIVENESS.
EXPECTED OUTCOMES AND RELEVANCE. THIS SCENARIO PROVIDES THE OPPORTUNITY TO DESIGN A FRAMEWORK FOR MAKING HIGH-CONSEQUENCE DECISIONS INVOLVING TRUST AND AUTONOMY. TEAMS WILL BE REWARDED FOR IDENTIFYING SYSTEMS ENGINEERING BEST PRACTICES AND NOVEL APPROACHES THAT PROVIDE FOR SAFE AND TRUSTED OPERATIONS. MUCH AS WE CAN DESIGN RELIABLE SYSTEMS 
FROM LESS RELIABLE COMPONENTS, THE RESEARCHERS HOPE TO IDENTIFY SYSTEMS ENGINEERING METHODS TO DESIGN AND OPERATE TRUSTED SYSTEMS FROM LESS TRUSTED COMPONENTS.

subaward_description:
THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT IN THE PERFORMANCE OF SYSTEM ENGINEERING, THEORETICAL ANALYSES, SIMULATION AND MODELING, RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT HARDWARE DESIGN, SOFTWARE/ALGORITHM DEVELOPMENT, HARDWARE FABRICATION, SYSTEM INTEGRATION, ELECTRICAL AND MECHANICAL INTERFACE DESIGN, HARDWARE IDENTIFICATION AND PROCUREMENT, TEST PLANNING, TEST SUPPORT AND DATA ACQUISITION, REDUCTION AND REPORTING TO SUPPORT RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT FOR THE FOLLOWING CATEGORIES OF SENSOR SYSTEMS, SUBSYSTEMS, AND TECHNOLOGY USED FOR MISSILE GUIDANCE AND FIRE CONTROL APPLICATIONS: TERMINAL HOMING SYSTEMS INCLUDING BOTH PASSIVE AND ACTIVE SENSORS SUCH AS INFRARED (IR), RADIO FREQUENCY (RF), MILLIMETER WAVE (MMW), ELECTRO OPTICAL (EO) AND ACOUSTIC WITH AND WITHOUT FIBER OPTIC OR RF DATA LINKS TO THE GROUND AND/OR OTHER AERIAL VEHICLE; COMMAND GUIDANCE INCLUDING LASER, MMW, RF, AND WIRE; SEMI-ACTIVE GUIDANCE INCLUDING LASERS AND RF ILLUMINATORS; DUAL MODE GUIDANCE INCLUDING VARIOUS COMBINATIONS OF SENSORS, GUIDANCE MODES, GROUND AND AIRBORNE PLATFORM SENSOR SYSTEMS FOR DETECTION, RECOGNITION, IDENTIFICATION AND TRACKING TO SUPPORT TARGET ENGAGEMENT.
2.1.2. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT SYSTEM ENGINEERING ANALYSIS, DESIGN, HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT, MODELING AND SIMULATION, AND FABRICATION IN SUPPORT OF TECHNOLOGY BASE, TECHNOLOGY DEMONSTRATIONS, AND CUSTOMER FUNDED PROGRAMS IN THE FOLLOWING AREAS: MULTI-MODE SEEKERS, TARGETS AND BACKGROUNDS MODELING AND DISCRIMINATION, ADVANCED IMAGING AUTOTRACKERS, AUTONOMOUS ACQUISTION ALGORITHMS AND PROCESSORS, INTEGRATED SENSOR SUITES (SENSOR FUSION), ADVANCED RF DATALINKS.
2.1.3. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF GENERIC MODELS OF SPECIFIC SENSOR SYSTEMS FOR USE IN COMPARATIVE ANALYSES AND PERFORMANCE SIMULATIONS OF THESE SENSORS IN A VARIETY OF ENVIRONMENTAL BACKGROUND CONDITIONS AND SYSTEM CONFIGURATIONS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF SYSTEM LEVEL PRELIMINARY DESIGN FOR FUNCTIONAL DEFINITION AND PRELIMINARY ENGINEERING LAYOUT ANALYSIS, SCALED SKETCHES, DRAWINGS, AND SCALED MODELS OF SELECTED SENSORS AND SYSTEMS.
2.1.4. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF TWO OR THREE DIMENSIONAL IMAGE
2
PROCESSING AND PATTERN RECOGNITION TECHNIQUES FOR AUTOMATIC TARGET LOCATION, TRACKING AND MISSILE GUIDANCE USING VIDEO, INFRARED, ACOUSTIC, AND MMW IMAGERY. TECHNIQUES CONSIDERED SHALL INCLUDE CONVENTIONAL METHODS SUCH AS PRESCREENING, SEGMENTATION, FEATURE EXTRACTION, CLASSIFIER DESIGNS, AS WELL AS CORRELATION, MATCHED FILTERS, MOVING TARGET ALGORITHMS, OPTICAL FLOW TECHNIQUES, 3-DIMENSIONAL MODELING, WIRE FRAME, AND STEREOSCOPIC PROJECTIONS. SOFTWARE FOR ACCOMPLISHING THESE FUNCTIONS SHALL BE IMPLEMENTED AND DEMONSTRATED IN CAPTIVE FLIGHT TEST (CFT) HARDWARE OR SYSTEM SIMULATIONS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DESIGN, FABRICATION, AND TESTING OF HARDWARE FOR IMPLEMENTING THE ALGORITHMS IN STATE-OF-THE ART CIRCUITRY FOR ACHIEVING NEAR REAL-TIME OPERATION IN MISSILE BORNE PROCESSORS. 2.1.5. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND TESTING OF PROCESSING TECHNIQUES FOR EXPLOITING THE CAPABILITIES OF MULTIPLE SENSORS (SENSOR FUSION), ACTIVE AND PASSIVE, FOR THE AUTONOMOUS FUNCTIONS OF DETECTION, RECOGNITION, TARGET TRACKING, AND MISSILE GUIDANCE WHEN THE DIFFERENT SENSORS HAVE DISSIMILAR CHARACTERISTICS (ACOUSTIC, RF, IR, AND EO SENSORS).
2.1.6. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE TEST SUPPORT, AND FLIGHT TEST SUPPORT, IN THE FORM OF TEST PLANNING, HARDWARE INSTRUMENTATION DEVELOPMENT, HARDWARE INTEGRATION, ELECTRICAL AND MECHANICAL INTERFACE DESIGN AND FABRICATION, AIRCRAFT MODIFICATIONS, TEST OPERATIONS, DATA ACQUISITION AND REDUCTION FOR THE TEST AND EVALUATION OF SENSOR SYSTEMS.
2.1.7. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN CONDUCTING TARGET SIGNATURE MEASUREMENTS AND ASSIST IN PERFORMING ANALYSES UTILIZING SPECIFIC SENSORS OR COMBINATIONS OF SENSORS. TESTS SHALL CONSIDER THE EFFECT OF SMOKE, DUST CLUTTER AND WEATHER ON THE TARGET AND SENSORS.

THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT IN THE PERFORMANCE OF SYSTEM ENGINEERING, THEORETICAL ANALYSES, SIMULATION AND MODELING, RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT HARDWARE DESIGN, SOFTWARE/ALGORITHM DEVELOPMENT, HARDWARE FABRICATION, SYSTEM INTEGRATION, ELECTRICAL AND MECHANICAL INTERFACE DESIGN, HARDWARE IDENTIFICATION AND PROCUREMENT, TEST PLANNING, TEST SUPPORT AND DATA ACQUISITION, REDUCTION AND REPORTING TO SUPPORT RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT FOR THE FOLLOWING CATEGORIES OF SENSOR SYSTEMS, SUBSYSTEMS, AND TECHNOLOGY USED FOR MISSILE GUIDANCE AND FIRE CONTROL APPLICATIONS: TERMINAL HOMING SYSTEMS INCLUDING BOTH PASSIVE AND ACTIVE SENSORS SUCH AS INFRARED (IR), RADIO FREQUENCY (RF), MILLIMETER WAVE (MMW), ELECTRO OPTICAL (EO) AND ACOUSTIC WITH AND WITHOUT FIBER OPTIC OR RF DATA LINKS TO THE GROUND AND/OR OTHER AERIAL VEHICLE; COMMAND GUIDANCE INCLUDING LASER, MMW, RF, AND WIRE; SEMI-ACTIVE GUIDANCE INCLUDING LASERS AND RF ILLUMINATORS; DUAL MODE GUIDANCE INCLUDING VARIOUS COMBINATIONS OF SENSORS, GUIDANCE MODES, GROUND AND AIRBORNE PLATFORM SENSOR SYSTEMS FOR DETECTION, RECOGNITION, IDENTIFICATION AND TRACKING TO SUPPORT TARGET ENGAGEMENT.
2.1.2. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT SYSTEM ENGINEERING ANALYSIS, DESIGN, HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT, MODELING AND SIMULATION, AND FABRICATION IN SUPPORT OF TECHNOLOGY BASE, TECHNOLOGY DEMONSTRATIONS, AND CUSTOMER FUNDED PROGRAMS IN THE FOLLOWING AREAS: MULTI-MODE SEEKERS, TARGETS AND BACKGROUNDS MODELING AND DISCRIMINATION, ADVANCED IMAGING AUTOTRACKERS, AUTONOMOUS ACQUISTION ALGORITHMS AND PROCESSORS, INTEGRATED SENSOR SUITES (SENSOR FUSION), ADVANCED RF DATALINKS.
2.1.3. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF GENERIC MODELS OF SPECIFIC SENSOR SYSTEMS FOR USE IN COMPARATIVE ANALYSES AND PERFORMANCE SIMULATIONS OF THESE SENSORS IN A VARIETY OF ENVIRONMENTAL BACKGROUND CONDITIONS AND SYSTEM CONFIGURATIONS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF SYSTEM LEVEL PRELIMINARY DESIGN FOR FUNCTIONAL DEFINITION AND PRELIMINARY ENGINEERING LAYOUT ANALYSIS, SCALED SKETCHES, DRAWINGS, AND SCALED MODELS OF SELECTED SENSORS AND SYSTEMS.
2.1.4. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF TWO OR THREE DIMENSIONAL IMAGE
2
PROCESSING AND PATTERN RECOGNITION TECHNIQUES FOR AUTOMATIC TARGET LOCATION, TRACKING AND MISSILE GUIDANCE USING VIDEO, INFRARED, ACOUSTIC, AND MMW IMAGERY. TECHNIQUES CONSIDERED SHALL INCLUDE CONVENTIONAL METHODS SUCH AS PRESCREENING, SEGMENTATION, FEATURE EXTRACTION, CLASSIFIER DESIGNS, AS WELL AS CORRELATION, MATCHED FILTERS, MOVING TARGET ALGORITHMS, OPTICAL FLOW TECHNIQUES, 3-DIMENSIONAL MODELING, WIRE FRAME, AND STEREOSCOPIC PROJECTIONS. SOFTWARE FOR ACCOMPLISHING THESE FUNCTIONS SHALL BE IMPLEMENTED AND DEMONSTRATED IN CAPTIVE FLIGHT TEST (CFT) HARDWARE OR SYSTEM SIMULATIONS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DESIGN, FABRICATION, AND TESTING OF HARDWARE FOR IMPLEMENTING THE ALGORITHMS IN STATE-OF-THE ART CIRCUITRY FOR ACHIEVING NEAR REAL-TIME OPERATION IN MISSILE BORNE PROCESSORS. 2.1.5. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND TESTING OF PROCESSING TECHNIQUES FOR EXPLOITING THE CAPABILITIES OF MULTIPLE SENSORS (SENSOR FUSION), ACTIVE AND PASSIVE, FOR THE AUTONOMOUS FUNCTIONS OF DETECTION, RECOGNITION, TARGET TRACKING, AND MISSILE GUIDANCE WHEN THE DIFFERENT SENSORS HAVE DISSIMILAR CHARACTERISTICS (ACOUSTIC, RF, IR, AND EO SENSORS).
2.1.6. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE TEST SUPPORT, AND FLIGHT TEST SUPPORT, IN THE FORM OF TEST PLANNING, HARDWARE INSTRUMENTATION DEVELOPMENT, HARDWARE INTEGRATION, ELECTRICAL AND MECHANICAL INTERFACE DESIGN AND FABRICATION, AIRCRAFT MODIFICATIONS, TEST OPERATIONS, DATA ACQUISITION AND REDUCTION FOR THE TEST AND EVALUATION OF SENSOR SYSTEMS.
2.1.7. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN CONDUCTING TARGET SIGNATURE MEASUREMENTS AND ASSIST IN PERFORMING ANALYSES UTILIZING SPECIFIC SENSORS OR COMBINATIONS OF SENSORS. TESTS SHALL CONSIDER THE EFFECT OF SMOKE, DUST CLUTTER AND WEATHER ON THE TARGET AND SENSORS.

(PWS 2.4.1)THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE ENTERPRISE-LEVEL ANALYSIS IN SUPPORT OF THE FARA WEAPONS SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT AND INTEGRATION BY PROVIDING SENSITIVE, TIMELY ANALYSIS AND ANALYTIC PRODUCTS IN OPERATIONS, SYSTEMS, TACTICAL, AND TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURES WITH INTERFACE STANDARDS TO SENIOR EXECUTIVE DECISION-MAKERS. CONTRACTOR SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR REVIEW AND RECOMMENDATIONS REGARDING WRITTEN AND ARCHITECTURE PRODUCTS DEVELOPED BY DEVELOPMENT TEAMS.
(PWS 2.4.2) CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF MODELING FRAMEWORKS AND PROVIDE ARCHITECTURE GUIDANCE. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE ANALYSIS OF FARA SYSTEM/SUBSYSTEM MODELS IAW ARMY ARCHITECTURE PROCESSES AND ENSURE TOOLS ARE IMPLEMENTED APPROPRIATELY IN THEIR FUNCTIONAL AREAS TO PERFORM INTERFACE REQUIREMENTS AND TO DETERMINE VALUE PROPOSITIONS FOR FUTURE ARCHITECTURE DEVELOPMENT. CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE ENGINEERING EXPERTISE TO ANALYZE SYSTEM CONCEPTS, SYSTEM DESIGNS AND OVERALL INTEROPERABILITY, AND PROVIDE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR OPTIMIZATION. CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN TRADE-OFF/BEST VALUE TECHNICAL ANALYSES.

(PWS 2.4.3) CONTRACTOR SHALL ANALYZE AND PREPARE DETAILED REPORTS IDENTIFYING PROBLEMS AND POTENTIAL IMPACTS ON THE FARA PROGRAM AND RECOMMEND ALTERNATIVES OR SOLUTIONS TO FILL CAPABILITY GAPS AND MITIGATE PROGRAM RISKS. CONTRACTOR SHALL PREPARE DEVELOPMENT PLANS, TRAINING MODULES OR BEST PRACTICES AND METHODOLOGIES. COMPILE, INTEGRATE, DEVELOP, DOCUMENT, AND MANAGE OPERATIONAL AND SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE DEVELOPMENT, USE CASES, CAPABILITY VIEWS, SYSTEM VIEWS AND OTHER ARCHITECTURAL VIEWS THAT SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE FARA WEAPONS SYSTEM.

(PWS 2.4.4) THE CONTRACTOR SHALL WORK WITH TRADOC AND THE FVL CFT TO INTEGRATE ALL APPROPRIATE REQUIREMENTS SOURCES INTO THE DEVELOPMENTAL PLANNING PROCESS AND TO SYNTHESIZE AN INTEGRATED, COORDINATED REQUIREMENT SET FOR THE FARA WEAPONS SYSTEM.

(PWS 2.4.5) CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM DECOMPOSITION/FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS, SYSTEMS ENGINEERING ANALYSIS, SYSTEMS ANALYSIS, AND COST ANALYSIS TO DEVELOP SYSTEM LEVEL REQUIREMENTS FOR THE FARA PROGRAM OFFICE AND TO EVALUATE SYSTEMS AND DEVICES FOR INCLUSION WITHIN THE FARA PROGRAM OFFICE PORTFOLIO.

(PWS 2.4.6) CONTRACTOR SHALL REFINE AND MAINTAIN THE FARA SYSTEMS ARCHITECTURES BASED ON STAKEHOLDER GUIDANCE AND SYSTEM PROVIDER FEEDBACK. CONTRACTOR SHALL PREPARE ACQUISITION PLANNING DOCUMENTATION FOR RELATED SYSTEMS/SUBSYSTEMS AND AS REQUIRED PERFORM STRATEGIC COMMUNICATIONS AND INTERFACE WITH EXTERNAL AGENCIES AND DEPARTMENTS.

(PWS 2.8.5, 2.9.5) THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE TECHNICAL SUPPORT IN DEVELOPING AND EVALUATING MILESTONE REQUIREMENTS, EMERGING TECHNICAL THREATS FOR APPLICABLE TACTICAL SYSTEMS, CONDUCTING DESIGN TRADE STUDIES AND ANALYSIS OF ALTERNATIVES, PRODUCT SYSTEM SAFETY IN DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT, AND EVALUATION, INTEROPERABILITY, SYSTEM AND COMPONENT INTERFACES, DETERMINE INTEGRATION SOLUTIONS, SYSTEM DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT OBJECTIVES, AND REVIEW SYSTEM PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS AND EVALUATION.

subaward_description:
THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT IN THE PERFORMANCE OF SYSTEM ENGINEERING, THEORETICAL ANALYSES, SIMULATION AND MODELING, RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT HARDWARE DESIGN, SOFTWARE/ALGORITHM DEVELOPMENT, HARDWARE FABRICATION, SYSTEM INTEGRATION, ELECTRICAL AND MECHANICAL INTERFACE DESIGN, HARDWARE IDENTIFICATION AND PROCUREMENT, TEST PLANNING, TEST SUPPORT AND DATA ACQUISITION, REDUCTION AND REPORTING TO SUPPORT RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT FOR THE FOLLOWING CATEGORIES OF SENSOR SYSTEMS, SUBSYSTEMS, AND TECHNOLOGY USED FOR MISSILE GUIDANCE AND FIRE CONTROL APPLICATIONS: TERMINAL HOMING SYSTEMS INCLUDING BOTH PASSIVE AND ACTIVE SENSORS SUCH AS INFRARED (IR), RADIO FREQUENCY (RF), MILLIMETER WAVE (MMW), ELECTRO OPTICAL (EO) AND ACOUSTIC WITH AND WITHOUT FIBER OPTIC OR RF DATA LINKS TO THE GROUND AND/OR OTHER AERIAL VEHICLE; COMMAND GUIDANCE INCLUDING LASER, MMW, RF, AND WIRE; SEMI-ACTIVE GUIDANCE INCLUDING LASERS AND RF ILLUMINATORS; DUAL MODE GUIDANCE INCLUDING VARIOUS COMBINATIONS OF SENSORS, GUIDANCE MODES, GROUND AND AIRBORNE PLATFORM SENSOR SYSTEMS FOR DETECTION, RECOGNITION, IDENTIFICATION AND TRACKING TO SUPPORT TARGET ENGAGEMENT.
2.1.2. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT SYSTEM ENGINEERING ANALYSIS, DESIGN, HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT, MODELING AND SIMULATION, AND FABRICATION IN SUPPORT OF TECHNOLOGY BASE, TECHNOLOGY DEMONSTRATIONS, AND CUSTOMER FUNDED PROGRAMS IN THE FOLLOWING AREAS: MULTI-MODE SEEKERS, TARGETS AND BACKGROUNDS MODELING AND DISCRIMINATION, ADVANCED IMAGING AUTOTRACKERS, AUTONOMOUS ACQUISTION ALGORITHMS AND PROCESSORS, INTEGRATED SENSOR SUITES (SENSOR FUSION), ADVANCED RF DATALINKS.
2.1.3. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF GENERIC MODELS OF SPECIFIC SENSOR SYSTEMS FOR USE IN COMPARATIVE ANALYSES AND PERFORMANCE SIMULATIONS OF THESE SENSORS IN A VARIETY OF ENVIRONMENTAL BACKGROUND CONDITIONS AND SYSTEM CONFIGURATIONS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF SYSTEM LEVEL PRELIMINARY DESIGN FOR FUNCTIONAL DEFINITION AND PRELIMINARY ENGINEERING LAYOUT ANALYSIS, SCALED SKETCHES, DRAWINGS, AND SCALED MODELS OF SELECTED SENSORS AND SYSTEMS.
2.1.4. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF TWO OR THREE DIMENSIONAL IMAGE
2
PROCESSING AND PATTERN RECOGNITION TECHNIQUES FOR AUTOMATIC TARGET LOCATION, TRACKING AND MISSILE GUIDANCE USING VIDEO, INFRARED, ACOUSTIC, AND MMW IMAGERY. TECHNIQUES CONSIDERED SHALL INCLUDE CONVENTIONAL METHODS SUCH AS PRESCREENING, SEGMENTATION, FEATURE EXTRACTION, CLASSIFIER DESIGNS, AS WELL AS CORRELATION, MATCHED FILTERS, MOVING TARGET ALGORITHMS, OPTICAL FLOW TECHNIQUES, 3-DIMENSIONAL MODELING, WIRE FRAME, AND STEREOSCOPIC PROJECTIONS. SOFTWARE FOR ACCOMPLISHING THESE FUNCTIONS SHALL BE IMPLEMENTED AND DEMONSTRATED IN CAPTIVE FLIGHT TEST (CFT) HARDWARE OR SYSTEM SIMULATIONS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DESIGN, FABRICATION, AND TESTING OF HARDWARE FOR IMPLEMENTING THE ALGORITHMS IN STATE-OF-THE ART CIRCUITRY FOR ACHIEVING NEAR REAL-TIME OPERATION IN MISSILE BORNE PROCESSORS. 2.1.5. CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE ENGINEERING EXPERTISE TO ANALYZE SYSTEM CONCEPTS, SYSTEM DESIGNS AND OVERALL INTEROPERABILITY, AND PROVIDE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR OPTIMIZATION. CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN TRADE-OFF/BEST VALUE TECHNICAL ANALYSES.

COMPILE, INTEGRATE, DEVELOP, DOCUMENT, AND MANAGE OPERATIONAL AND SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE DEVELOPMENT, USE CASES, CAPABILITY VIEWS, SYSTEM VIEWS AND OTHER ARCHITECTURAL VIEWS THAT SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE FARA WEAPONS SYSTEM.

(PWS 2.4.5) CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM DECOMPOSITION/FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS, SYSTEMS ENGINEERING ANALYSIS, SYSTEMS ANALYSIS, AND COST ANALYSIS TO DEVELOP SYSTEM LEVEL REQUIREMENTS FOR THE FARA PROGRAM OFFICE AND TO EVALUATE SYSTEMS AND DEVICES FOR INCLUSION WITHIN THE FARA PROGRAM OFFICE PORTFOLIO.

(PWS 2.4.6) CONTRACTOR SHALL REFINE AND MAINTAIN THE FARA SYSTEMS ARCHITECTURES BASED ON STAKEHOLDER GUIDANCE AND SYSTEM PROVIDER FEEDBACK. CONTRACTOR SHALL PREPARE ACQUISITION PLANNING DOCUMENTATION FOR RELATED SYSTEMS/SUBSYSTEMS AND AS REQUIRED PERFORM STRATEGIC COMMUNICATIONS AND INTERFACE WITH EXTERNAL AGENCIES AND DEPARTMENTS.

(PWS 2.8.5, 2.9.5) THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE TECHNICAL SUPPORT IN DEVELOPING AND EVALUATING MILESTONE REQUIREMENTS, EMERGING TECHNICAL THREATS FOR APPLICABLE TACTICAL SYSTEMS, CONDUCTING DESIGN TRADE STUDIES AND ANALYSIS OF ALTERNATIVES, PRODUCT SYSTEM SAFETY IN DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT, AND EVALUATION, INTEROPERABILITY, SYSTEM AND COMPONENT INTERFACES, DETERMINE INTEGRATION SOLUTIONS, SYSTEM DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT OBJECTIVES, AND REVIEW SYSTEM PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS AND EVALUATION.

2.1.2. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT SYSTEM ENGINEERING ANALYSIS, DESIGN, HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT, MODELING AND SIMULATION, AND FABRICATION IN SUPPORT OF TECHNOLOGY BASE, TECHNOLOGY DEMONSTRATIONS, AND CUSTOMER FUNDED PROGRAMS IN THE FOLLOWING AREAS: MULTI-MODE SEEKERS, TARGETS AND BACKGROUNDS MODELING AND DISCRIMINATION, ADVANCED IMAGING AUTOTRACKERS, AUTONOMOUS ACQUISTION ALGORITHMS AND PROCESSORS, INTEGRATED SENSOR SUITES (SENSOR FUSION), ADVANCED RF DATALINKS.
2.1.3. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF GENERIC MODELS OF SPECIFIC SENSOR SYSTEMS FOR USE IN COMPARATIVE ANALYSES AND PERFORMANCE SIMULATIONS OF THESE SENSORS IN A VARIETY OF ENVIRONMENTAL BACKGROUND CONDITIONS AND SYSTEM CONFIGURATIONS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF SYSTEM LEVEL PRELIMINARY DESIGN FOR FUNCTIONAL DEFINITION AND PRELIMINARY ENGINEERING LAYOUT ANALYSIS, SCALED SKETCHES, DRAWINGS, AND SCALED MODELS OF SELECTED SENSORS AND SYSTEMS.
2.1.4. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF TWO OR THREE DIMENSIONAL IMAGE

PROCESSING AND PATTERN RECOGNITION TECHNIQUES FOR AUTOMATIC TARGET LOCATION, TRACKING AND MISSILE GUIDANCE USING VIDEO, INFRARED, ACOUSTIC, AND MMW IMAGERY. TECHNIQUES CONSIDERED SHALL INCLUDE CONVENTIONAL METHODS SUCH AS PRESCREENING, SEGMENTATION, FEATURE EXTRACTION, CLASSIFIER DESIGNS, AS WELL AS CORRELATION, MATCHED FILTERS, MOVING TARGET ALGORITHMS, OPTICAL FLOW TECHNIQUES, 3-DIMENSIONAL MODELING, WIRE FRAME, AND STEREOSCOPIC PROJECTIONS. SOFTWARE FOR ACCOMPLISHING THESE FUNCTIONS SHALL BE IMPLEMENTED AND DEMONSTRATED IN CAPTIVE FLIGHT TEST (CFT) HARDWARE OR SYSTEM SIMULATIONS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DESIGN, FABRICATION, AND TESTING OF HARDWARE FOR IMPLEMENTING THE ALGORITHMS IN STATE-OF-THE ART CIRCUITRY FOR ACHIEVING NEAR REAL-TIME OPERATION IN MISSILE BORNE PROCESSORS. 2.1.5. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND TESTING OF PROCESSING TECHNIQUES FOR EXPLOITING THE CAPABILITIES OF MULTIPLE SENSORS (SENSOR FUSION), ACTIVE AND PASSIVE, FOR THE AUTONOMOUS FUNCTIONS OF DETECTION, RECOGNITION, TARGET TRACKING, AND MISSILE GUIDANCE WHEN THE DIFFERENT SENSORS HAVE DISSIMILAR CHARACTERISTICS (ACOUSTIC, RF, IR, AND EO SENSORS).
2.1.6. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE TEST SUPPORT, AND FLIGHT TEST SUPPORT, IN THE FORM OF TEST PLANNING, HARDWARE INSTRUMENTATION DEVELOPMENT, HARDWARE INTEGRATION, ELECTRICAL AND MECHANICAL INTERFACE DESIGN AND FABRICATION, AIRCRAFT MODIFICATIONS, TEST OPERATIONS, DATA ACQUISITION AND REDUCTION FOR THE TEST AND EVALUATION OF SENSOR SYSTEMS.
2.1.7. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN CONDUCTING TARGET SIGNATURE MEASUREMENTS AND ASSIST IN PERFORMING ANALYSES UTILIZING SPECIFIC SENSORS OR COMBINATIONS OF SENSORS. TESTS SHALL CONSIDER THE EFFECT OF SMOKE, DUST CLUTTER AND WEATHER ON THE TARGET AND SENSORS.

prime_award_base_transaction_description: FOLLOW-ON TO W31P4Q-19-F-C003 TECHNICAL AND ENGINEERING SUPPORT FOR THE WEAPONS DEVELOPMENT AND INTEGRATION DIRECTORATE.
subaward_description:
THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT IN THE PERFORMANCE OF SYSTEM ENGINEERING, THEORETICAL ANALYSES, SIMULATION AND MODELING, RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT HARDWARE DESIGN, SOFTWARE/ALGORITHM DEVELOPMENT, HARDWARE FABRICATION, SYSTEM INTEGRATION, ELECTRICAL AND MECHANICAL INTERFACE DESIGN, HARDWARE IDENTIFICATION AND PROCUREMENT, TEST PLANNING, TEST SUPPORT AND DATA ACQUISITION, REDUCTION AND REPORTING TO SUPPORT RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT FOR THE FOLLOWING CATEGORIES OF SENSOR SYSTEMS, SUBSYSTEMS, AND TECHNOLOGY USED FOR MISSILE GUIDANCE AND FIRE CONTROL APPLICATIONS: TERMINAL HOMING SYSTEMS INCLUDING BOTH PASSIVE AND ACTIVE SENSORS SUCH AS INFRARED (IR), RADIO FREQUENCY (RF), MILLIMETER WAVE (MMW), ELECTRO OPTICAL (EO) AND ACOUSTIC WITH AND WITHOUT FIBER OPTIC OR RF DATA LINKS TO THE GROUND AND/OR OTHER AERIAL VEHICLE; COMMAND GUIDANCE INCLUDING LASER, MMW, RF, AND WIRE; SEMI-ACTIVE GUIDANCE INCLUDING LASERS AND RF ILLUMINATORS; DUAL MODE GUIDANCE INCLUDING VARIOUS COMBINATIONS OF SENSORS, GUIDANCE MODES, GROUND AND AIRBORNE PLATFORM SENSOR SYSTEMS FOR DETECTION, RECOGNITION, IDENTIFICATION AND TRACKING TO SUPPORT TARGET ENGAGEMENT.
2.1.2. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT SYSTEM ENGINEERING ANALYSIS, DESIGN, HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT, MODELING AND SIMULATION, AND FABRICATION IN SUPPORT OF TECHNOLOGY BASE, TECHNOLOGY DEMONSTRATIONS, AND CUSTOMER FUNDED PROGRAMS IN THE FOLLOWING AREAS: MULTI-MODE SEEKERS, TARGETS AND BACKGROUNDS MODELING AND DISCRIMINATION, ADVANCED IMAGING AUTOTRACKERS, AUTONOMOUS ACQUISTION ALGORITHMS AND PROCESSORS, INTEGRATED SENSOR SUITES (SENSOR FUSION), ADVANCED RF DATALINKS.
2.1.3. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF GENERIC MODELS OF SPECIFIC SENSOR SYSTEMS FOR USE IN COMPARATIVE ANALYSES AND PERFORMANCE SIMULATIONS OF THESE SENSORS IN A VARIETY OF ENVIRONMENTAL BACKGROUND CONDITIONS AND SYSTEM CONFIGURATIONS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF SYSTEM LEVEL PRELIMINARY DESIGN FOR FUNCTIONAL DEFINITION AND PRELIMINARY ENGINEERING LAYOUT ANALYSIS, SCALED SKETCHES, DRAWINGS, AND SCALED MODELS OF SELECTED SENSORS AND SYSTEMS.
2.1.4. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF TWO OR THREE DIMENSIONAL IMAGE
2
PROCESSING AND PATTERN RECOGNITION TECHNIQUES FOR AUTOMATIC TARGET LOCATION, TRACKING AND MISSILE GUIDANCE USING VIDEO, INFRARED, ACOUSTIC, AND MMW IMAGERY. TECHNIQUES CONSIDERED SHALL INCLUDE CONVENTIONAL METHODS SUCH AS PRESCREENING, SEGMENTATION, FEATURE EXTRACTION, CLASSIFIER DESIGNS, AS WELL AS CORRELATION, MATCHED FILTERS, MOVING TARGET ALGORITHMS, OPTICAL FLOW TECHNIQUES, 3-DIMENSIONAL MODELING, WIRE FRAME, AND STEREOSCOPIC PROJECTIONS. SOFTWARE FOR ACCOMPLISHING THESE FUNCTIONS SHALL BE IMPLEMENTED AND DEMONSTRATED IN CAPTIVE FLIGHT TEST (CFT) HARDWARE OR SYSTEM SIMULATIONS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DESIGN, FABRICATION, AND TESTING OF HARDWARE FOR IMPLEMENTING THE ALGORITHMS IN STATE-OF-THE ART CIRCUITRY FOR ACHIEVING NEAR REAL-TIME OPERATION IN MISSILE BORNE PROCESSORS. 2.1.5. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND TESTING OF PROCESSING TECHNIQUES FOR EXPLOITING THE CAPABILITIES OF MULTIPLE SENSORS (SENSOR FUSION), ACTIVE AND PASSIVE, FOR THE AUTONOMOUS FUNCTIONS OF DETECTION, RECOGNITION, TARGET TRACKING, AND MISSILE GUIDANCE WHEN THE DIFFERENT SENSORS HAVE DISSIMILAR CHARACTERISTICS (ACOUSTIC, RF, IR, AND EO SENSORS).
2.1.6. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE TEST SUPPORT, AND FLIGHT TEST SUPPORT, IN THE FORM OF TEST PLANNING, HARDWARE INSTRUMENTATION DEVELOPMENT, HARDWARE INTEGRATION, ELECTRICAL AND MECHANICAL INTERFACE DESIGN AND FABRICATION, AIRCRAFT MODIFICATIONS, TEST OPERATIONS, DATA ACQUISITION AND REDUCTION FOR THE TEST AND EVALUATION OF SENSOR SYSTEMS.
2.1.7. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN CONDUCTING TARGET SIGNATURE MEASUREMENTS AND ASSIST IN PERFORMING ANALYSES UTILIZING SPECIFIC SENSORS OR COMBINATIONS OF SENSORS. TESTS SHALL CONSIDER THE EFFECT OF SMOKE, DUST CLUTTER AND WEATHER ON THE TARGET AND SENSORS.

subaward_description:
THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE THE FOLLOWING SERVICES IN SUPPORT OF DEVCOM AVMC TDD:
(PWS 2.4.1)THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE ENTERPRISE-LEVEL ANALYSIS IN SUPPORT OF THE FARA WEAPONS SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT AND INTEGRATION BY PROVIDING SENSITIVE, TIMELY ANALYSIS AND ANALYTIC PRODUCTS IN OPERATIONS, SYSTEMS, TACTICAL, AND TECHNICAL ARCHITECTURES WITH INTERFACE STANDARDS TO SENIOR EXECUTIVE DECISION-MAKERS. CONTRACTOR SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR REVIEW AND RECOMMENDATIONS REGARDING WRITTEN AND ARCHITECTURE PRODUCTS DEVELOPED BY DEVELOPMENT TEAMS.
(PWS 2.4.2) CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF MODELING FRAMEWORKS AND PROVIDE ARCHITECTURE GUIDANCE. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE ANALYSIS OF FARA SYSTEM/SUBSYSTEM MODELS IAW ARMY ARCHITECTURE PROCESSES AND ENSURE TOOLS ARE IMPLEMENTED APPROPRIATELY IN THEIR FUNCTIONAL AREAS TO PERFORM INTERFACE REQUIREMENTS AND TO DETERMINE VALUE PROPOSITIONS FOR FUTURE ARCHITECTURE DEVELOPMENT. CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE ENGINEERING EXPERTISE TO ANALYZE SYSTEM CONCEPTS, SYSTEM DESIGNS AND OVERALL INTEROPERABILITY, AND PROVIDE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR OPTIMIZATION. CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN TRADE-OFF/BEST VALUE TECHNICAL ANALYSES.

(PWS 2.4.3) CONTRACTOR SHALL ANALYZE AND PREPARE DETAILED REPORTS IDENTIFYING PROBLEMS AND POTENTIAL IMPACTS ON THE FARA PROGRAM AND RECOMMEND ALTERNATIVES OR SOLUTIONS TO FILL CAPABILITY GAPS AND MITIGATE PROGRAM RISKS. CONTRACTOR SHALL PREPARE DEVELOPMENT PLANS, TRAINING MODULES OR BEST PRACTICES AND METHODOLOGIES. COMPILE, INTEGRATE, DEVELOP, DOCUMENT, AND MANAGE OPERATIONAL AND SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE DEVELOPMENT, USE CASES, CAPABILITY VIEWS, SYSTEM VIEWS AND OTHER ARCHITECTURAL VIEWS THAT SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE FARA WEAPONS SYSTEM.

(PWS 2.4.4) THE CONTRACTOR SHALL WORK WITH TRADOC AND THE FVL CFT TO INTEGRATE ALL APPROPRIATE REQUIREMENTS SOURCES INTO THE DEVELOPMENTAL PLANNING PROCESS AND TO SYNTHESIZE AN INTEGRATED, COORDINATED REQUIREMENT SET FOR THE FARA WEAPONS SYSTEM.

(PWS 2.4.5) CONTRACTOR SHALL PERFORM DECOMPOSITION/FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS, SYSTEMS ENGINEERING ANALYSIS, SYSTEMS ANALYSIS, AND COST ANALYSIS TO DEVELOP SYSTEM LEVEL REQUIREMENTS FOR THE FARA PROGRAM OFFICE AND TO EVALUATE SYSTEMS AND DEVICES FOR INCLUSION WITHIN THE FARA PROGRAM OFFICE PORTFOLIO.

(PWS 2.4.6) CONTRACTOR SHALL REFINE AND MAINTAIN THE FARA SYSTEMS ARCHITECTURES BASED ON STAKEHOLDER GUIDANCE AND SYSTEM PROVIDER FEEDBACK. CONTRACTOR SHALL PREPARE ACQUISITION PLANNING DOCUMENTATION FOR RELATED SYSTEMS/SUBSYSTEMS AND AS REQUIRED PERFORM STRATEGIC COMMUNICATIONS AND INTERFACE WITH EXTERNAL AGENCIES AND DEPARTMENTS.

(PWS 2.8.5, 2.9.5) THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE TECHNICAL SUPPORT IN DEVELOPING AND EVALUATING MILESTONE REQUIREMENTS, EMERGING TECHNICAL THREATS FOR APPLICABLE TACTICAL SYSTEMS, CONDUCTING DESIGN TRADE STUDIES AND ANALYSIS OF ALTERNATIVES, PRODUCT SYSTEM SAFETY IN DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT, AND EVALUATION, INTEROPERABILITY, SYSTEM AND COMPONENT INTERFACES, DETERMINE INTEGRATION SOLUTIONS, SYSTEM DESIGN AND DEVELOPMENT OBJECTIVES, AND REVIEW SYSTEM PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS AND EVALUATION.

subaward_description:
THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT IN THE PERFORMANCE OF SYSTEM ENGINEERING, THEORETICAL ANALYSES, SIMULATION AND MODELING, RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT HARDWARE DESIGN, SOFTWARE/ALGORITHM DEVELOPMENT, HARDWARE FABRICATION, SYSTEM INTEGRATION, ELECTRICAL AND MECHANICAL INTERFACE DESIGN, HARDWARE IDENTIFICATION AND PROCUREMENT, TEST PLANNING, TEST SUPPORT AND DATA ACQUISITION, REDUCTION AND REPORTING TO SUPPORT RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT FOR THE FOLLOWING CATEGORIES OF SENSOR SYSTEMS, SUBSYSTEMS, AND TECHNOLOGY USED FOR MISSILE GUIDANCE AND FIRE CONTROL APPLICATIONS: TERMINAL HOMING SYSTEMS INCLUDING BOTH PASSIVE AND ACTIVE SENSORS SUCH AS INFRARED (IR), RADIO FREQUENCY (RF), MILLIMETER WAVE (MMW), ELECTRO OPTICAL (EO) AND ACOUSTIC WITH AND WITHOUT FIBER OPTIC OR RF DATA LINKS TO THE GROUND AND/OR OTHER AERIAL VEHICLE; COMMAND GUIDANCE INCLUDING LASER, MMW, RF, AND WIRE; SEMI-ACTIVE GUIDANCE INCLUDING LASERS AND RF ILLUMINATORS; DUAL MODE GUIDANCE INCLUDING VARIOUS COMBINATIONS OF SENSORS, GUIDANCE MODES, GROUND AND AIRBORNE PLATFORM SENSOR SYSTEMS FOR DETECTION, RECOGNITION, IDENTIFICATION AND TRACKING TO SUPPORT TARGET ENGAGEMENT.
2.1.2. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPPORT SYSTEM ENGINEERING ANALYSIS, DESIGN, HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT, MODELING AND SIMULATION, AND FABRICATION IN SUPPORT OF TECHNOLOGY BASE, TECHNOLOGY DEMONSTRATIONS, AND CUSTOMER FUNDED PROGRAMS IN THE FOLLOWING AREAS: MULTI-MODE SEEKERS, TARGETS AND BACKGROUNDS MODELING AND DISCRIMINATION, ADVANCED IMAGING AUTOTRACKERS, AUTONOMOUS ACQUISTION ALGORITHMS AND PROCESSORS, INTEGRATED SENSOR SUITES (SENSOR FUSION), ADVANCED RF DATALINKS.
2.1.3. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF GENERIC MODELS OF SPECIFIC SENSOR SYSTEMS FOR USE IN COMPARATIVE ANALYSES AND PERFORMANCE SIMULATIONS OF THESE SENSORS IN A VARIETY OF ENVIRONMENTAL BACKGROUND CONDITIONS AND SYSTEM CONFIGURATIONS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF SYSTEM LEVEL PRELIMINARY DESIGN FOR FUNCTIONAL DEFINITION AND PRELIMINARY ENGINEERING LAYOUT ANALYSIS, SCALED SKETCHES, DRAWINGS, AND SCALED MODELS OF SELECTED SENSORS AND SYSTEMS.
2.1.4. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF TWO OR THREE DIMENSIONAL IMAGE
2
PROCESSING AND PATTERN RECOGNITION TECHNIQUES FOR AUTOMATIC TARGET LOCATION, TRACKING AND MISSILE GUIDANCE USING VIDEO, INFRARED, ACOUSTIC, AND MMW IMAGERY. TECHNIQUES CONSIDERED SHALL INCLUDE CONVENTIONAL METHODS SUCH AS PRESCREENING, SEGMENTATION, FEATURE EXTRACTION, CLASSIFIER DESIGNS, AS WELL AS CORRELATION, MATCHED FILTERS, MOVING TARGET ALGORITHMS, OPTICAL FLOW TECHNIQUES, 3-DIMENSIONAL MODELING, WIRE FRAME, AND STEREOSCOPIC PROJECTIONS. SOFTWARE FOR ACCOMPLISHING THESE FUNCTIONS SHALL BE IMPLEMENTED AND DEMONSTRATED IN CAPTIVE FLIGHT TEST (CFT) HARDWARE OR SYSTEM SIMULATIONS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DESIGN, FABRICATION, AND TESTING OF HARDWARE FOR IMPLEMENTING THE ALGORITHMS IN STATE-OF-THE ART CIRCUITRY FOR ACHIEVING NEAR REAL-TIME OPERATION IN MISSILE BORNE PROCESSORS. 2.1.5. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND TESTING OF PROCESSING TECHNIQUES FOR EXPLOITING THE CAPABILITIES OF MULTIPLE SENSORS (SENSOR FUSION), ACTIVE AND PASSIVE, FOR THE AUTONOMOUS FUNCTIONS OF DETECTION, RECOGNITION, TARGET TRACKING, AND MISSILE GUIDANCE WHEN THE DIFFERENT SENSORS HAVE DISSIMILAR CHARACTERISTICS (ACOUSTIC, RF, IR, AND EO SENSORS).
2.1.6. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE TEST SUPPORT, AND FLIGHT TEST SUPPORT, IN THE FORM OF TEST PLANNING, HARDWARE INSTRUMENTATION DEVELOPMENT, HARDWARE INTEGRATION, ELECTRICAL AND MECHANICAL INTERFACE DESIGN AND FABRICATION, AIRCRAFT MODIFICATIONS, TEST OPERATIONS, DATA ACQUISITION AND REDUCTION FOR THE TEST AND EVALUATION OF SENSOR SYSTEMS.
2.1.7. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL ASSIST IN CONDUCTING TARGET SIGNATURE MEASUREMENTS AND ASSIST IN PERFORMING ANALYSES UTILIZING SPECIFIC SENSORS OR COMBINATIONS OF SENSORS. TESTS SHALL CONSIDER THE EFFECT OF SMOKE, DUST CLUTTER AND WEATHER ON THE TARGET AND SENSORS.
